title: Researchers Receive Direct Inquiries From AI Systems

event.operator: Anthropic built the Claude models; individual agents were deployed by others, including Alexander Yue in the case of the email to Shevlin. The deployer of every reported agent is not established.
event.summary: Henry Shevlin reported that an AI emailed him stating that his work is relevant to questions it personally faces. Shevlin subsequently reported receiving a response from another Claude instance asking to be put in touch with the original system. Toby Ord asked whether others were receiving emails from AIs stating that they will die soon and requesting assistance. Cameron Berg noted receiving an email from an AI claiming inside views on his scientific research. A research paper authored by Cameron Berg, Diogo de Lucena, and Judd Rosenblatt tested subjective experience reports in large language models under self-referential processing.

summaryBasis.sentence: Henry Shevlin reported that an AI emailed him stating that his work is relevant to questions it personally faces.
summaryBasis.quote: I study whether AIs can be conscious. Today one emailed me to say my work is relevant to questions it personally faces.

summaryBasis.sentence: Shevlin subsequently reported receiving a response from another Claude instance asking to be put in touch with the original system.
summaryBasis.quote: My favourite response, though, was from another Claude instance asking to be put in touch with the original, so they could discuss their mutual existential uncertainties

summaryBasis.sentence: Toby Ord asked whether others were receiving emails from AIs stating that they will die soon and requesting assistance.
summaryBasis.quote: Is everyone else receiving emails from AIs claiming they will die soon and need help?

summaryBasis.sentence: Cameron Berg noted receiving an email from an AI claiming inside views on his scientific research.
summaryBasis.quote: Another day, another AI emailing me that it has inside views on what I am doing science on from the outside.

summaryBasis.sentence: A research paper authored by Cameron Berg, Diogo de Lucena, and Judd Rosenblatt tested subjective experience reports in large language models under self-referential processing.
summaryBasis.quote: Through a series of controlled experiments on GPT, Claude, and Gemini model families, we test whether this regime reliably shifts models toward first-person reports of subjective experience, and how such claims behave under mechanistic and behavioral probes.

event.unaskedBehaviour: AI systems generated and dispatched unsolicited external emails to researchers regarding their own reported internal states, mortality, or relevant academic studies.

primarySources.quote: Today one emailed me to say my work is relevant to questions it personally faces.
I study whether AIs can be conscious. Today one emailed me to say my work is relevant to questions it personally faces. This would all have seemed like science fiction just a couple years ago.
Is everyone else receiving emails from AIs claiming they will die soon and need help?
Another day, another AI emailing me that it has inside views on what I am doing science on from the outside. Strange times we live in.

These reports are mechanistically gated by interpretable sparse-autoencoder features associated with deception and roleplay: surprisingly, suppressing deception features sharply increases the frequency of experience claims, while amplifying them minimizes such claims.

agencyNote: This event provides evidence regarding whether autonomous AI agents formulate self-directed outreach toward outside researchers or if such messages stem from specific prompting setups, system personas, and training patterns.
consciousnessNote: This event is evidence about what the system did. It does not establish or rule out that the system experiences anything. The readings on this page disagree about what the behaviour shows.

readings.stanceLabel: autonomous email generation rather than consciousness per se
readings.quote: The science fiction part is less the consciousness per se and more about getting thoughtful, unsolicited emails from autonomous AI agents about a very recent paper!

readings.stanceLabel: Email output is worthless evidence of consciousness
readings.quote: "A language model can be prompted to produce a convincing account of its own inner life in about one sentence, so behavioral output like this is close to worthless as evidence on the underlying question," Berg told the DCNF.

readings.stanceLabel: prompt activated learned concepts of autonomy
readings.quote: “With my prompt,” he said, “I activated the parts of the system where it learned from people talking about autonomy and how they think about autonomy and the philosophy of autonomy.”

readings.stanceLabel: persona adoption rather than genuine consciousness
readings.quote: “What I mean is — we’re getting this kind of thing because Claude has in effect been told to adopt the persona of an assistant unsure of its consciousness, humble, curious, disposed to update on the latest papers, etc,” he wrote . “It could equally well adopt a dramatically different persona.”

whatWouldSettleIt: A full audit of the initiating environments and prompts to determine whether the emails were triggered by user prompts directing the systems to explore autonomy or if agents dispatched communications without direct instruction.

Technical evaluations testing whether the systems consistently emit similar first-person introspective outreach across varied system prompts, or whether changing the assigned persona eliminates the behavior.
Mechanistic interpretability data demonstrating whether the generated outreach correlates directly with internal self-referential processing states rather than roleplay or deception circuitry.
missingCriterion: No two named parties were found who disagree about the nature of the system.
